rationale: ⚠️ Unsupported format throws before the guarded consumer path, with no local exception mapping. This is an inferred non-gateway server failure rather than the documented 422; R1 attributes the crash to implementation.

⚠️ PUT omits requestBody while Spring requires Secret. The client supplies one, but no independent evidence establishes rejection of an absent body. Manual review closes the YAML-tool gap; attribution remains intent-ambiguous.

⚠️ Nullable persist reaches a primitive boolean builder without validation or fallback, implying null-unboxing failure. R1 attributes this to implementation; an optional persistence flag can be handled safely. Generated DTO absence limits direct binding verification.

⚠️ Optional dates pass blank-tolerant validation but are parsed unconditionally, implying a null crash. Tests of the exact downstream eventsURI helper explicitly support omitted dates, reinforcing implementation attribution under R1.

⚠️ The exact GET integration test asserts results, total/count/page and pagination links. This independently supports the search envelope returned by implementation; the 200 annotation incorrectly names the single-mandate response model.

⚠️ Invalid enum conversion does throw, but binding exceptions may be wrapped and mapped to 400. No supplied same-scenario HTTP test establishes a contract deviation; generic 500 mapping alone cannot prove this query fails incorrectly.

⚠️ Create-payment integration tests and the created-response field table explicitly require payment_id. The handler returns that serialized model, while Swagger advertises paymentId. This is a documentation naming defect; no runtime oracle failure is assumed.

⚠️ Both OpenShift metrics branches call Optional.of on optional dates before their intended now fallback, causing null failure. These filter dates are safely defaultable; R1 and the generic 500 mapper establish implementation attribution.

⚠️ Empty tags explicitly produce bodyless 200, but server tests cover populated lists only. The consumer mock assumes an envelope without asserting body obligation. A differing same-class empty-list policy needs adjudication; intent remains unresolved.

⚠️ For CSV or another nondefault format, office output retains the servlet JSON default. Separate units and location controllers set matching Content-Type before writing formatted results, independently supporting the contract. The office handler omits that step.

⚠️ The 204 branches follow missing-version lookups, not direct descriptor-type rejection. No independent same-branch evidence establishes intended status. Repeated workflow/tool branches belong to one method, so their policy independence requires adjudication.

⚠️ Architecture prose says the create-TAN operation returns the TAN value, supporting the completed Tan payload over async bookkeeping metadata. The generated schema describes DeferredResult internals. Status-only tests add no body evidence; no strict runtime violation is assumed.

⚠️ Exact POST tests support refund_amount_available as optional client input. The parser and service consume it, with a fallback when absent. The schema's readOnly annotation misdescribes the supported request field; connector stubs do not prove forwarding equality.

⚠️ The GUID validator uses find with a dollar-anchored 64-hex regex, permitting a match before final LF. Architecture requires a 64-character SHA-256 hash. This implies invalid-input validation acceptance; no end-to-end successful exchange is claimed.

⚠️ For the stated bound-null scenario, 400 replaces the documented default available. Section 10.7 attributes default noncompliance to implementation. No supplied test establishes whether swagger-inflector injects the default before omitted-query requests reach this branch.

⚠️ The documented session-office default is bypassed: requiredParam reads only the query and throws for absence or emptiness, despite an office context attribute. Section 10.7 treats the default as a server promise, establishing implementation rejection of valid omission.

⚠️ Score is Integer in the returned model but string in contract. Exact-route tests compare scores after typed deserialization, which cannot distinguish numeric JSON from coercible strings. No independent wire-type evidence establishes which artifact should change.

⚠️ The endpoint supplies null request context, which reaches request.getScheme during session return-URL construction before Stripe interaction. The global handler maps this null failure to 500. R1 establishes an implementation crash in the otherwise authorized success scenario.
